title: e2e: do not modify the caller's URL in OpenWebSocketForURL
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind flake
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`OpenWebSocketForURL` in the e2e framework rewrote the scheme of the `*url.URL` it was given in place: `https` became `wss`, anything else became `ws`. On a second call with the same URL the scheme was already `wss`, which is not `https`, so it was turned into plain `ws` and the dial sent plaintext HTTP to the TLS port. Go's HTTP server answers that with `400 Bad Request` before the request reaches any handler, and the websocket client reports it as `bad status`.

The "Pods should support retrieving logs from the container over websockets" conformance test builds the URL once and retries the websocket read with `gomega.Eventually`. Whenever the first attempt succeeded but the container had not flushed `container is alive` yet, every retry failed with `bad status` until the 2 minute timeout. That is exactly the signature in #142284:

- the apiserver log shows one `CONNECT .../log?container=main` with `hijacked=true` and nothing afterwards, and the kubelet served that one `/containerLogs` request with 200;
- Gomega's message ends with "At one point, however, the function did return successfully" and an empty string.

The helper now works on a copy of the URL and treats `wss` like `https`, so repeated calls behave like the first. The other callers (`exec` over websockets in the same file and `kubectl port-forward` websocket test) call the helper once and are unaffected.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142284

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The new unit test starts an `httptest` TLS server with a websocket handler and dials it three times with the same URL. Before the fix, the second attempt fails with `websocket.Dial ws://127.0.0.1:...: bad status` and the server logs `client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server`, the same pair of messages as in the failing CI runs.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```
